column1: # The PKZIP 1.01/1.02 minimum-match-length bug, in the writer's own
# distribution archive. Found by CONTENT, by a key for the WRITER: the
# first 16 bytes of a PKSFX 1.01/1.02 self-extractor are its stub's DOS
# EXE header, 4d5a98001f000b002000c10affff0a0e, the same bytes in 1.01
# and 1.02 and different in 1.10 — so `detection=` names every
# self-extractor those two versions wrote, where no token about a zip's
# own first bytes can see one at all (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-08).
# PKZ101.EXE is PKZIP 1.01's July 1989 distribution, imploded by the
# version it ships. Three of its thirteen entries decode to the stored
# CRC-32 only under the DICTIONARY-SIZE minimum match length and not
# under APPNOTE.TXT 5.3.4: README.DOC, ORDER.DOC and OMBUDSMN.ASP, each
# at flags 0x0004 — a 4 K dictionary with three trees. deark adjudicates
# ("MML bug detection: 1"); `unar` and Info-ZIP `unzip` fail the same
# three on CRC, as does this engine.
# Freely re-fetchable, so it is fixture-eligible: the same bytes are on
# at least six Discmaster items. A second pinned copy, sha256 identical:
#   https://discmaster.textfiles.com/file/1969/RBBSIABOX31.cdr/pool/pkz101.exe
# and four more the sweep found, all with the same three entries:
#   /file/29622/ibm0040-0049/ibm0043.tar/ibm0043/FRACTUN1.ZIP/FRACTUNE/PKZ101.EXE
#   /file/29986/wbiz0020-0029/wbiz0022.tar/wbiz0022/PKZ101.EXE
#   /file/41140/ClubHouseBBS.zip/ClubHouseBBS/PKZ101.EXE
# The two NEGATIVE controls are here because they are what makes the
# find mean something: PKZ102.EXE is the other buggy version and writes
# no bug-capable entry at all, and PKZ110.EXE is the version that fixed
# the bug and is where "version made by" turns from 1.0 into 1.1.
# FORMATS.md, *Implode*, has the figures.
# name
implode-PKZ101
implode-PKZ102
implode-PKZ110
